messages.subject: Basic syntax for lagged effects
parts:
I have panel data which consists of two time periods. Obviously, the values of many variables at time t will be dependent on previous values of those variables.

As an example, let's say that tax compliance in period t-1 affects penalties for tax evasion in period t (the government adjusts their policy based on previous levels of compliance).

From http://lavaan.ugent.be or the previously asked questions, is not completely clear to me how I should specify this in the model, apart from simply putting it in the regression.

In addition, values of tax compliance will be dependent on its own previous values. Do I need to specify this as well, and if so, how?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Basic syntax for lagged effects
parts:
These don't sound like lavaan questions, but basic SEM questions.  You read up on panel models in longitudinal SEM textbooks such as Little (2013) or Newsom (2015).  SEMNET is a good resource for posting general questions about SEM.

https://listserv.ua.edu/cgi-bin/wa?SUBED1=semnet&A=1
